BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.

IMPORTANT (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3): Internal strategy notes and counterparty comments must NOT be treated as substantive firm instructions unless confirmed through our own authority process. From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every material point. Several departures are structural. Folding Title into the general regime, extending limitations to "all Claims of any nature", deemed disclosure of the whole data room, and a blanket buyer-knowledge bar would together remove most of our protection, including against fraud. We should reject the package as framed and mark up against our starting positions.

The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts several claims in its Update draft (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Sandbar). We should use that.

---

## A. Structural issues (highest priority)

### 1. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **What it means:** As drafted, this covers fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct. Fraud claims would be capped at AUD 4.8m, time-barred at 18 months, subject to the basket, and potentially defeated by non-reliance.
- **Playbook:** The fraud carve-out applies to everything, to the maximum extent enforceable, and no one may waive it.
- **Push back:** Insert an express carve-out. Nothing in cl 9.3, 12, 13 or 20.5, or any other limitation, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance provision, limits liability for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct by the Seller or its representatives. This is non-negotiable.

### 2. Hidden general-regime override (cl 12.3 / 13)
- **What it means:** "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" makes the general regime the default for every category: Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants. Any category we fail to carve out expressly falls into it.
- **Playbook:** Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate, with no hidden override.
- **Push back:** Delete it. Limitations should apply only to General Warranty Claims as defined. Each other category should have its own express regime, and payment obligations and covenants should be outside the limitations altogether.

### 3. Capacity and Title folded into the general caps and time limits
- **What it means:** On a 100% share purchase, title is the whole deal. A AUD 4.8m cap on a AUD 24m title failure is unacceptable. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason.
- **Playbook:** A separate Fundamental regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Push back:** Reject outright and restore the Fundamental regime.

### 4. General disclosure of the data room and public registers (Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2], Schedule 7)
- **What it means:** Everything in DD-002 to DD-012, the Accounts, the statutory registers and public records would qualify every warranty, whether or not the issue was fairly identified against a specific warranty.
- **Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only, and reject whole-data-room, public-register or deemed disclosure.
- **Push back:** Delete [1.1] and [1.2]. Disclosures should qualify a warranty only where they are made specifically against it, with enough detail for us to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Also note that [1.1] is fixed at 22 September 2026, about six weeks ago. Any disclosure must be brought down to signing and Completion, and repeated warranties must not be qualified by unfiled updates.

### 5. Buyer-knowledge bar (cl 8.3)
- **What it means:** We would have no claim for anything we or our advisers knew, or anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. Combined with item 4, this would effectively eliminate warranty protection for any issue we diligenced, including the DD-002 to DD-012 matters we are negotiating protection for.
- **Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Push back:** Delete cl 8.3. If the Seller insists on a knowledge concept, it should operate only on the Seller's side (named persons, after reasonable enquiry). It must expressly not affect Title, capacity, fraud claims or the specific indemnities, which exist precisely because we know about those matters.

---

## B. Economic terms

### 6. General cap of 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1)
- **Playbook:** Our starting position is 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% is a conditional fallback that needs prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft. We have none.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller's number matches our fallback, but that does not make it cleared. A matching number is not authority. This draft also bundles the cap with materially worse terms in items 1–5, 7 and 8. The cap would apply to a much wider set of claims than our fallback assumed, so even with authority the fallback's premise would not hold.
- **Push back:** Hold at 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not signal 20% as acceptable. Any move should be escalated to Amelia Frost with this draft identified and the bundled terms flagged.

### 7. Thresholds (cl 12.2)
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 |
| Basket | AUD 250,000 | AUD 50,000 |
| Basket type | Deductible (excess only) | Tipping (first dollar) |

- **Reasoning:** Each limb is 5x our position, and the deductible structure means we absorb the first AUD 250k permanently. Items under AUD 25k would not even count toward the basket.
- **Push back:** Restore AUD 5k / AUD 50k with a tipping basket. Confirm that de minimis claims of the same or related nature aggregate, and that Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific indemnity and fraud claims sit outside both thresholds.

### 8. General claims period of 18 months (cl 12.3)
- **Playbook:** 24 months. 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
- **Push back:** Hold at 24 months. Fundamental claims run at least six years. Tax and IP periods remain open (see item 16).

---

## C. Transaction-specific matters

### 9. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- **Contradiction:** The Update says the consent is "addressed". The Disclosure Letter (§2) says no final written consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Reasoning:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m and about 30% of FY26 revenue, a material customer. Under the Seller's draft, receiving a written consent letter would satisfy the condition even if Bluefen's cl 11.3 conditions were never met, so the consent might not be effective. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient.
- **Push back:** The Condition Precedent should require effective Bluefen consent under DD-002 cl 11.2, plus evidence satisfactory to the Buyer that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, both before Completion. Upgrade the obligation to all reasonable endeavours (or best endeavours) and remove the "satisfied on delivery" deeming. Completion should not occur on a conditional or unsatisfied consent without our written waiver.

### 10. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- **Contradiction:** The Disclosure (§3) confirms about AUD 3.2m is outstanding, not repaid, with no discharge, and the facility has a change-control clause (8.1).
- **Reasoning:** A post-Completion release leaves the Company's assets encumbered after we own it. It also risks a change-of-control default under cl 8.1, and on a debt-free/cash-free deal it shifts risk to us.
- **Push back:**
  - A current payout letter from Riverlark, dated close to Completion.
  - Direct repayment from Completion funds in the funds flow.
  - Effective releases (deeds of release, PPSR discharges, release of any real property or other security) delivered at Completion.
  - The amount treated as Debt in the price mechanics.
- **Fallback:** A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable lender undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. Neither is in place, so we should not offer it.

### 11. DD-005 employee bonuses (AUD 420,000) excluded from the funds flow
- **What it means:** The Seller's statement that the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics" sits alongside its own admission (Disclosure §5) that the bonuses are not in it. On-costs (payroll tax, superannuation and similar) are unaddressed. If the Company pays these after Completion, we bear them, and that is a silent price reduction.
- **Push back:** Either list AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs as a specific Completion line item (Debt / Transaction Costs deducted from price), or make them Seller-funded with an indemnity. The Seller should confirm the on-cost calculation. Do not accept "a matter for the Seller" without a mechanism.

### 12. Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)
- **Reasoning:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. An indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment" covers the fee but not the IP consequence: failure to obtain title to SOW3 materials, third-party claims, re-development cost, or business interruption. The AUD 180,000 open amount comes from DD-010 and is not independently verified. We should not assume it is correct, overstated or understated.
- **Push back:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover all Losses arising from any failure of the Company to own, or to have validly received, the Ironquay / SOW3 deliverables, and any Ironquay claim.
  - Preserve the SOW3 cure: as a Completion deliverable, the Seller procures payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees (with evidence of cleared payment) and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, or the amount is retained or escrowed.
  - Request bank and remittance evidence to verify the actual open balance.
  - Keep the indemnity outside the general cap, basket and time limits.

### 13. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6)
- **Reasoning:** The Seller's characterisation ("preliminary… not expected to be material") is an assertion, not a verified fact. Its own Disclosure (§6) says the scope, any access and any notification obligation are unknown. Equally, we should not treat it as a confirmed breach, assume harm or a notification duty, or put a number on it.
- **Push back:**
  - Interim covenants: preserve all logs and evidence, complete the investigation with appropriate forensic support, and give regular written updates before Completion, including on any notification assessment.
  - Do not let "not material" language enter the SPA or qualify warranties.
  - Seek a specific indemnity for Losses arising from the incident (regulatory, notification, third-party claims, remediation), outside the general limitations. Its scope should depend on the investigation findings, not on any assumed outcome.

### 14. Sandbar supplier renewals (AUD 330,000)
- **Reasoning:** The Seller calls these "ordinary-course operating costs", but its own Disclosure (§8) says it does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and that DD-008 and DD-011 should be read together. They are three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each.
- **Position:** Assess before agreeing any treatment. Confirm timing, scope, termination rights, whether they were pre-paid or accrued, whether they were entered into or renewed in contemplation of the sale, and whether they breach conduct-of-business restrictions. Do not accept the "ordinary course" label, and do not automatically classify them as Debt or seek a price deduction. Decide once the facts are in.

### 15. Title evidenced by DD-012 share register
- **Reasoning:** The register is an internal source supplied by the Seller. The Disclosure (§10) concedes that we have not verified it. It does not prove beneficial ownership, absence of encumbrances or authority.
- **Push back:** Require independent evidence:
  - ASIC company extract and historical searches reconciled to the register.
  - Issue and transfer history with stamped instruments where relevant.
  - PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company.
  - Confirmation of no options, convertibles or other rights over shares.
  - Seller board approvals and authority evidence.
  - Original share certificates and duly executed transfers at Completion.

  Title warranties stay in the Fundamental regime regardless.

### 16. Tax / IP "settled under the general regime"
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain open. Nothing has been agreed and neither side has assumed unlimited liability.
- **Push back:** Do not accept that these are settled. Reserve our position expressly. Tax and IP should be negotiated as separate categories, with their own caps, time periods and threshold treatment, outside the general regime. We have not agreed any outcome and should not concede general-regime treatment by silence.

---

## D. Lower-priority and verification points

- **Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009):** The Disclosure describes only a notification obligation and an assignment restriction, not a share-sale consent. These are probably not Conditions, but counsel should confirm against the actual clauses, since the Seller's description is not verification. Make lease notification a Completion deliverable and diligence any change-of-control drafting in Mossvale.
- **Disclosure Letter [1.4] non-admission:** Acceptable in principle, provided it does not undercut any specific indemnity or the Conditions. Add that nothing in the letter limits the specific indemnities, Fundamental or Tax claims.
- **Staleness:** The Disclosure is as at 22 September 2026. Request an updated letter and data-room index, and refreshed status on Bluefen, Riverlark, DD-006, Ironquay and Sandbar, distinguishing documented updates from Seller assertions.
- **Framing:** Characterisations such as "fair and balanced", "agreed price mechanics", "addressed" and "considered adequate" are the Seller's assertions. None reflects a concluded agreement or any authority on our side.

---

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject** the extension of limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims". Insert a full fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out (non-negotiable).
2. **Delete** the general-regime override in cl 12.3/13 and keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate.
3. **Restore** the Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge.
4. **Delete** general and deemed disclosure. Specific fair disclosure only, brought down to signing and Completion.
5. **Delete** the cl 8.3 buyer-knowledge bar.
6. **Hold** the cap at 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% is not authorised. Escalate to Amelia Frost only with this draft identified and the bundled terms flagged.
7. **Hold** thresholds at AUD 5k / AUD 50k with a tipping basket.
8. **Hold** the general claims period at 24 months. 18 months is not authorised.
9. **Bluefen:** effective consent plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied as a CP before Completion. No consent-on-delivery and no bare reasonable endeavours.
10. **Riverlark:** payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds and releases at Completion. No post-Completion release without an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
11. **Bonuses:** AUD 420k plus on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded.
12. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure (payment plus confirmatory assignment at Completion or retention), and verify the AUD 180k independently.
13. **DD-006:** preservation, investigation and update covenants, plus a specific indemnity. Assume neither breach nor immateriality.
14. **Sandbar:** diligence first, with no "ordinary course" acceptance and no automatic Debt classification.
15. **Title:** independent evidence beyond the DD-012 register.
16. **Tax/IP:** expressly reserved as open, not settled under the general regime.

**Escalation note for Amelia Frost:** No fallback (20% cap, 18-month period, post-Completion Riverlark release) is currently authorised, and this response should not offer any of them. If the team later wants to deploy one, it needs her prior written authority referencing this specific draft. That request should explain that the Seller has packaged these numbers with structural changes (items 1–5) that would make the fallbacks materially worse than they appear in isolation.

- **Push back:** The Condition Precedent should require effective Bluefen consent under DD-002 cl 11.2, plus evidence satisfactory to the Buyer that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, both before Completion. Upgrade the obligation to all reasonable endeavours (or best endeavours) and remove the "satisfied on delivery" deeming. Completion should not occur on a conditional or unsatisfied consent without our written waiver.

### 10. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- **Contradiction:** The Disclosure (§3) confirms about AUD 3.2m is outstanding, not repaid, with no discharge, and the facility has a change-control clause (8.1).

### 11. DD-005 employee bonuses (AUD 420,000) excluded from the funds flow
- **What it means:** The Seller's statement that the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics" sits alongside its own admission (Disclosure §5) that the bonuses are not in it. On-costs (payroll tax, superannuation and similar) are unaddressed. If the Company pays these after Completion, we bear them, and that is a silent price reduction.

- **Reasoning:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. An indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment" covers the fee but not the IP consequence: failure to obtain title to SOW3 materials, third-party claims, re-development cost, or business interruption. The AUD 180,000 open amount comes from DD-010 and is not independently verified. We should not assume it is correct, overstated or understated.

### 13. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6)
- **Reasoning:** The Seller's characterisation ("preliminary… not expected to be material") is an assertion, not a verified fact. Its own Disclosure (§6) says the scope, any access and any notification obligation are unknown. ### 14. Sandbar supplier renewals (AUD 330,000)
- **Reasoning:** The Seller calls these "ordinary-course operating costs", but its own Disclosure (§8) says it does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and that DD-008 and DD-011 should be read together. They are three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each.

Confirm timing, scope, termination rights, whether they were pre-paid or accrued, whether they were entered into or renewed in contemplation of the sale, and whether they breach conduct-of-business restrictions. ### 15. Title evidenced by DD-012 share register
- **Reasoning:** The register is an internal source supplied by the Seller. The Disclosure (§10) concedes that we have not verified it. It does not prove beneficial ownership, absence of encumbrances or authority.

### 16. Tax / IP "settled under the general regime"
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain open. Nothing has been agreed and neither side has assumed unlimited liability.
- **Push back:** Do not accept that these are settled. Reserve our position expressly. Tax and IP should be negotiated as separate categories, with their own caps, time periods and threshold treatment, outside the general regime. We have not agreed any outcome and should not concede general-regime treatment by silence.

1. **Reject** the extension of limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims". Insert a full fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out (non-negotiable).
2. **Delete** the general-regime override in cl 12.3/13 and keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate.
3. **Restore** the Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge.
4. **Delete** general and deemed disclosure. Specific fair disclosure only, brought down to signing and Completion.
5. **Delete** the cl 8.3 buyer-knowledge bar.
6. **Hold** the cap at 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% is not authorised. Escalate to Amelia Frost only with this draft identified and the bundled terms flagged.
7. **Hold** thresholds at AUD 5k / AUD 50k with a tipping basket.
8. **Hold** the general claims period at 24 months. 18 months is not authorised.
9. **Bluefen:** effective consent plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied as a CP before Completion. No consent-on-delivery and no bare reasonable endeavours.
